Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Brick breaker game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java collision fixture and testability contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward, y increases downward, negative vy is upward, and positive vy is downward
- Paddle's x value is the horizontal CENTER, not its left edge: getX() returns that center, asRect() has left edge x-width/2.0, and setX clamps the center to [width/2.0,maxX-width/2.0]; for Paddle(100.0,180.0,80.0,10.0,200.0), getX() is exactly 100.0 and asRect() spans x=60.0 through 140.0
- Game has the exact injectable constructor Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); it defensively copies the list but retains the supplied Ball, Paddle, and Brick object identities so deterministic tests can observe mutation
- Game declares the life counter exactly as private int lives; final, effectively immutable, shadow, record, or alternate life counters are forbidden; the constructor assigns this.lives = lives and getLives() returns that same mutable field
- bottom-out handling is exact: when ball.getY()+ball.getRadius()>=height and lives>0, execute lives -= 1 exactly once, set lifeLost=true, reset the retained ball to x=paddle.getX() and y=paddle.getY()-ball.getRadius()-1.0, and make its vertical velocity negative; an implementation that only sets lifeLost without decrementing lives is forbidden

src/main/java/Rect.java: public final class Rect { public final double x; public final double y; public final double width; public final double height; public Rect(double x, double y, double width, double height); public double left(); public double top(); public double right(); public double bottom(); Semantics: immutable AABB defined by top-left x,y and size. left()=x, top()=y, right()=x+width, bottom()=y+height.

src/main/java/Ball.java: public final class Ball { private double x,y,vx,vy,radius; public Ball(double x, double y, double vx, double vy, double radius); public double getX(); public double getY(); public double getVx(); public double getVy(); public double getRadius(); void setPosition(double x, double y); void setVelocity(double vx, double vy); Semantics: setPosition and setVelocity are package-private (no access modifier) for tests; getters return current state; radius>0 invariant is assumed. No internal clamping.

src/main/java/Paddle.java: public final class Paddle { private double x,y,width,height,maxX; public Paddle(double x, double y, double width, double height, double maxX); public double getX(); public double getY(); public double getWidth(); public double getHeight(); public void setX(double x); public Rect asRect(); Semantics: paddle uses center semantics (x,y at center). setX clamps the center x to [width/2, maxX - width/2]. asRect() returns Rect with top-left at (x - width/2, y - height/2) and same width/height.

src/main/java/Brick.java: public final class Brick { private final Rect rect; private int hitPoints; private final boolean breakable; public Brick(Rect rect, int hitPoints, boolean breakable); public Rect getRect(); public int getHitPoints(); public boolean isBreakable(); public void hit(); public boolean isDestroyed(); Semantics: hit() decrements hitPoints by 1 if hitPoints>0 and always leaves hitPoints >= 0. isDestroyed() returns hitPoints == 0. Non-breakable bricks can be destroyed logically (hitPoints can reach 0) but are not removed nor scored by Game.

src/main/java/Collision.java: public final class Collision { public static boolean circleIntersectsRect(double cx, double cy, double r, Rect rect); public static double[] penetration(double cx, double cy, double r, Rect rect); Semantics: Inclusive intersection: returns true if the distance from (cx,cy) to the rect is <= r. Implementation uses nearest-point-on-rect clamping and squared distance check. penetration() requires that an intersection exists; it returns new double[]{penX, penY} where penX = max(0, r - abs(cx - clamp(cx, rect.left(), rect.right()))), penY = max(0, r - abs(cy - clamp(cy, rect.top(), rect.bottom()))). These are magnitudes only. Callers choose the axis with the smaller magnitude to reflect velocity. In exact ties, callers may prefer Y-axis reflection for determinism.

src/main/java/Game.java: public final class Game { private final double width,height; private final Paddle paddle; private final Ball ball; private final java.util.List<Brick> bricks; private int lives; int score; boolean levelCompleted; boolean lifeLost; public Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); public int getLives(); public boolean isLifeLost(); public boolean isLevelCompleted(); public int getScore(); public java.util.List<Brick> getBricks(); public Paddle getPaddle(); public Ball getBall(); public void tick(double dt); Semantics and rules: - Constructor: stores width/height; keeps references to the given paddle and ball; makes a defensive copy of the provided bricks list while retaining object identities, in insertion order; lives>=0. getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view of the internal list. - tick(dt): Validates dt is finite and > 0; otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException. On each call, resets lifeLost=false. Integrates the ball exactly once: ball.x += ball.vx * dt; ball.y += ball.vy * dt. Collision processing order: (1) walls (left/right/top reflection, bottom-out life loss), (2) paddle, (3) bricks (first-hit only). Walls: inclusive checks against bounds [0,width]x[0,height]. Left/right: if ball.x - r <= 0 reflect vx = -vx and clamp ball.x = r; if ball.x + r >= width reflect vx and clamp ball.x = width - r. Top: if ball.y - r <= 0 reflect vy and clamp ball.y = r. Bottom-out: if ball.y - r >= height then a life is lost: decrement lives exactly by 1 (but not below 0), set lifeLost=true, and reset ball state as follows: position x := paddle.getX(), y := paddle.getY() - paddle.getHeight()/2 - ball.getRadius() (exactly tangent above the paddle); velocity vx := 0; vy := -Math.abs(previous vy). No further collisions are processed in this tick when bottom-out occurs. Paddle collision: compute paddleRect = paddle.asRect(); if Collision.circleIntersectsRect(ball.x,ball.y,r,paddleRect) reflect along min-penetration axis. Resolution: obtain {penX,penY} = Collision.penetration(...). If penY <= penX reflect vertical (vy = -vy) and translate ball out along Y by penY in the sign away from the paddle; else reflect horizontal (vx = -vx) and translate along X accordingly. Bricks collision: iterate over a snapshot copy of the bricks list and handle the first brick for which there is an intersection similarly: reflect along min-penetration axis, call brick.hit(), and if brick.isBreakable() and brick.isDestroyed() then remove the brick from the internal list and increase score by exactly 100. Stop after handling the first colliding brick this tick. Level completion: levelCompleted is true iff all remaining bricks in the list are either non-breakable or destroyed (i.e., there are no remaining breakable and non-destroyed bricks). Flags and getters: getBricks() returns an unmodifiable list; lifeLost reflects only the outcome of the most recent tick; score is cumulative; getLives() returns current lives.

src/main/java/Main.java: public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); Semantics: constructs a tiny deterministic demo (e.g., a small world with a paddle, a ball, and zero or one brick), runs a single Game.tick with a fixed dt, and prints a single status line summarizing lives and score. No input reading, no GUI, and deterministic output.

Implementation uses nearest-point-on-rect clamping and squared distance check. penetration() requires that an intersection exists; it returns new double[]{penX, penY} where penX = max(0, r - abs(cx - clamp(cx, rect.left(), rect.right()))), penY = max(0, r - abs(cy - clamp(cy, rect.top(), rect.bottom()))). In exact ties, callers may prefer Y-axis reflection for determinism.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java: public final class Game { private final double width,height; private final Paddle paddle; private final Ball ball; private final java.util.List<Brick> bricks; private int lives; int score; boolean levelCompleted; boolean lifeLost; public Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); public int getLives(); public boolean isLifeLost(); public boolean isLevelCompleted(); public int getScore(); public java.util.List<Brick> getBricks(); public Paddle getPaddle(); public Ball getBall(); public void tick(double dt); Semantics and rules: - Constructor: stores width/height; keeps references to the given paddle and ball; makes a defensive copy of the provided bricks list while retaining object identities, in insertion order; lives>=0. getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view of the internal list. - tick(dt): Validates dt is finite and > 0; otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException. Implementation uses nearest-point-on-rect clamping and squared distance check. penetration() requires that an intersection exists; it returns new double[]{penX, penY} where penX = max(0, r - abs(cx - clamp(cx, rect.left(), rect.right()))), penY = max(0, r - abs(cy - clamp(cy, rect.top(), rect.bottom()))). These are magnitudes only. Callers choose the axis with the smaller magnitude to reflect velocity. In exact ties, callers may prefer Y-axis reflection for determinism.

src/main/java/Game.java: public final class Game { private final double width,height; private final Paddle paddle; private final Ball ball; private final java.util.List<Brick> bricks; private int lives; int score; boolean levelCompleted; boolean lifeLost; public Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); public int getLives(); public boolean isLifeLost(); public boolean isLevelCompleted(); public int getScore(); public java.util.List<Brick> getBricks(); public Paddle getPaddle(); public Ball getBall(); public void tick(double dt); Semantics and rules: - Constructor: stores width/height; keeps references to the given paddle and ball; makes a defensive copy of the provided bricks list while retaining object identities, in insertion order; lives>=0. getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view of the internal list. - tick(dt): Validates dt is finite and > 0; otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException. On each call, resets lifeLost=false. Integrates the ball exactly once: ball.x += ball.vx * dt; ball.y += ball.vy * dt. Collision processing order: (1) walls (left/right/top reflection, bottom-out life loss), (2) paddle, (3) bricks (first-hit only). Walls: inclusive checks against bounds [0,width]x[0,height]. Left/right: if ball.x - r <= 0 reflect vx = -vx and clamp ball.x = r; if ball.x + r >= width reflect vx and clamp ball.x = width - r. Top: if ball.y - r <= 0 reflect vy and clamp ball.y = r. Bottom-out: if ball.y - r >= height then a life is lost: decrement lives exactly by 1 (but not below 0), set lifeLost=true, and reset ball state as follows: position x := paddle.getX(), y := paddle.getY() - paddle.getHeight()/2 - ball.getRadius() (exactly tangent above the paddle); velocity vx := 0; vy := -Math.abs(previous vy). No further collisions are processed in this tick when bottom-out occurs. Paddle collision: compute paddleRect = paddle.asRect(); if Collision.circleIntersectsRect(ball.x,ball.y,r,paddleRect) reflect along min-penetration axis. Resolution: obtain {penX,penY} = Collision.penetration(...). If penY <= penX reflect vertical (vy = -vy) and translate ball out along Y by penY in the sign away from the paddle; else reflect horizontal (vx = -vx) and translate along X accordingly. Bricks collision: iterate over a snapshot copy of the bricks list and handle the first brick for which there is an intersection similarly: reflect along min-penetration axis, call brick.hit(), and if brick.isBreakable() and brick.isDestroyed() then remove the brick from the internal list and increase score by exactly 100. Stop after handling the first colliding brick this tick. Level completion: levelCompleted is true iff all remaining bricks in the list are either non-breakable or destroyed (i.e., there are no remaining breakable and non-destroyed bricks). Flags and getters: getBricks() returns an unmodifiable list; lifeLost reflects only the outcome of the most recent tick; score is cumulative; getLives() returns current lives.

src/main/java/Main.java: public final class Main { public static void main(String[] args); Semantics: constructs a tiny deterministic demo (e.g., a small world with a paddle, a ball, and zero or one brick), runs a single Game.tick with a fixed dt, and prints a single status line summarizing lives and score. No input reading, no GUI, and deterministic output.

src/test/java/MainTest.java: JUnit 5 tests only. Tests import classes from the default package (no package declarations). Must not rely on GUI or timing. Covers: (1) Main.main runs without throwing; (2) one-brick fixture leads to brick removal, +100 score, and levelCompleted true; (3) life-loss fixture triggers at bottom-out, decrements lives once, sets lifeLost true, centers and positions ball exactly above paddle, and sets vx=0 and vy negative absolute of prior vy. Tests may access package-private Ball.setPosition and Ball.setVelocity to set up fixtures.

Import/include rules: tests reference only the declared classes; core modules must not depend on Main; Game may depend on Collision; entities may be used by Game; no other cross-module cycles.","Shared Knowledge":"Build with Maven; runtime entry is src/main/java/Main.java. Game.tick(dt) performs deterministic single-step integration and collision handling (walls, then paddle, then bricks), and enforces exact bottom-out life-loss/reset rules. Collision stays pure and stateless. Tests are headless and deterministic, use only JUnit Jupiter, and interact with default-package classes directly. getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view; Game holds a defensive copy of the bricks list.","Execution Protocol":"Build and run tests with: mvn -q test. Runtime entry is Main.main in src/main/java/Main.java; tests ensure it executes without error. No additional files alter protocol-prescribed files.","Anything UNCLEAR":""}

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Brick breaker game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java collision fixture and testability contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward, y increases downward, negative vy is upward, and positive vy is downward
- Paddle's x value is the horizontal CENTER, not its left edge: getX() returns that center, asRect() has left edge x-width/2.0, and setX clamps the center to [width/2.0,maxX-width/2.0]; for Paddle(100.0,180.0,80.0,10.0,200.0), getX() is exactly 100.0 and asRect() spans x=60.0 through 140.0
- Game has the exact injectable constructor Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); it defensively copies the list but retains the supplied Ball, Paddle, and Brick object identities so deterministic tests can observe mutation
- Game declares the life counter exactly as private int lives; final, effectively immutable, shadow, record, or alternate life counters are forbidden; the constructor assigns this.lives = lives and getLives() returns that same mutable field
- bottom-out handling is exact: when ball.getY()+ball.getRadius()>=height and lives>0, execute lives -= 1 exactly once, set lifeLost=true, reset the retained ball to x=paddle.getX() and y=paddle.getY()-ball.getRadius()-1.0, and make its vertical velocity negative; an implementation that only sets lifeLost without decrementing lives is forbidden
- getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view or copy and tests must never mutate that result to configure the game; tests needing one brick must invoke the injectable constructor with java.util.List.of(brick), never call createDemoLevel() and then assert or try to force a one-brick layout
- Ball exposes package-private setPosition(double x,double y) and setVelocity(double vx,double vy), accessible to the sole default-package MainTest; Brick.hit() decrements a breakable brick by exactly one to a minimum of zero
- tick(dt) validates finite dt>0, integrates x+=vx*dt and y+=vy*dt once, handles left/right/top walls, paddle, then bricks; a colliding brick is hit exactly once in that tick, a destroyed breakable brick is removed and adds exactly 100 score once, and levelCompleted becomes true exactly when the retained bricks list is empty
- circle/rectangle contact is inclusive: nearest-point squared distance <= radius squared is a collision; resolve on the minimum-penetration axis and reflect the corresponding velocity component
- the exact one-brick fixture is: width=200.0, height=200.0; Paddle(100.0,180.0,80.0,10.0,200.0); Ball(60.0,45.0,0.0,10.0,5.0); Brick(new Rect(50.0,50.0,20.0,10.0),1,true); lives=3; after tick(0.1), the same brick has 0 hit points, getBricks() is empty, score is 100, and levelCompleted is true
- the exact life-loss fixture uses the same dimensions and paddle, Ball(100.0,199.0,0.0,20.0,5.0), an unbreakable Brick(new Rect(0.0,20.0,20.0,10.0),1,false), and 3 lives; after tick(0.5), lives is 2, lifeLost is true, ball x is 100.0, ball y is 174.0, ball vy is negative, and levelCompleted is false because the unbreakable brick remains
- MainTest contains exactly three concise deterministic tests: Main.main smoke, the exact injected one-brick fixture, and the exact injected life-loss fixture; the two domain tests MUST copy every numeric constructor argument and dt above literally, with no alternate dimensions, positions, velocities, radius, paddle, brick, or time step
- MainTest's life test must literally assert assertEquals(2,game.getLives()), assertTrue(game.isLifeLost()), assertEquals(100.0,ball.getX(),1e-9), assertEquals(174.0,ball.getY(),1e-9), assertTrue(ball.getVy()<0.0), and assertFalse(game.isLevelCompleted()); approximate phrases such as "positioned to cross" are insufficient and alternative fixtures are forbidden
- MainTest's brick test must literally use the stated 200.0-world fixture and tick(0.1), then assert the same Brick identity has zero hit points, game.getBricks().isEmpty(), score 100, and levelCompleted true; createDemoLevel and any substituted fixture are forbidden in this test
- retained Brick identity means only that the caller's original `brick` reference observes brick.getHitPoints()==0 after Game mutates and removes it; after removal the brick list MUST NOT contain that object, so the test must use assertFalse(game.getBricks().contains(brick)); asserting both isEmpty() and contains(brick), or otherwise asserting contains(brick) after removal, is explicitly forbidden
- the Game.java task and Full API must spell the reset expression as ball.setPosition(paddle.getX(),paddle.getY()-ball.getRadius()-1.0); examples using -0.1, paddle.getX()+paddle.getWidth()/2.0, a preserved old ball x, or any alternative formula are forbidden
- repeat the exact constructor, center-based Paddle semantics, mutable private int lives field, mandatory lives -= 1 bottom-out statement and reset coordinates, retained entity identity observed through the external brick reference, mandatory assertFalse after brick removal, read-only brick list, tick order, inclusive collision, score/removal rule, bricks-empty completion rule, coordinate convention, literal test assertions, and both numeric fixtures in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 39 functions or methods
- about 628 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries

- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix

- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Brick breaker game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java collision fixture and testability contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward, y increases downward, negative vy is upward, and positive vy is downward
- Paddle's x value is the horizontal CENTER, not its left edge: getX() returns that center, asRect() has left edge x-width/2.0, and setX clamps the center to [width/2.0,maxX-width/2.0]; for Paddle(100.0,180.0,80.0,10.0,200.0), getX() is exactly 100.0 and asRect() spans x=60.0 through 140.0
- Game has the exact injectable constructor Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); it defensively copies the list but retains the supplied Ball, Paddle, and Brick object identities so deterministic tests can observe mutation
- Game declares the life counter exactly as private int lives; final, effectively immutable, shadow, record, or alternate life counters are forbidden; the constructor assigns this.lives = lives and getLives() returns that same mutable field
- bottom-out handling is exact: when ball.getY()+ball.getRadius()>=height and lives>0, execute lives -= 1 exactly once, set lifeLost=true, reset the retained ball to x=paddle.getX() and y=paddle.getY()-ball.getRadius()-1.0, and make its vertical velocity negative; an implementation that only sets lifeLost without decrementing lives is forbidden
- getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view or copy and tests must never mutate that result to configure the game; tests needing one brick must invoke the injectable constructor with java.util.List.of(brick), never call createDemoLevel() and then assert or try to force a one-brick layout
- Ball exposes package-private setPosition(double x,double y) and setVelocity(double vx,double vy), accessible to the sole default-package MainTest; Brick.hit() decrements a breakable brick by exactly one to a minimum of zero
- tick(dt) validates finite dt>0, integrates x+=vx*dt and y+=vy*dt once, handles left/right/top walls, paddle, then bricks; a colliding brick is hit exactly once in that tick, a destroyed breakable brick is removed and adds exactly 100 score once, and levelCompleted becomes true exactly when the retained bricks list is empty
- circle/rectangle contact is inclusive: nearest-point squared distance <= radius squared is a collision; resolve on the minimum-penetration axis and reflect the corresponding velocity component
- the exact one-brick fixture is: width=200.0, height=200.0; Paddle(100.0,180.0,80.0,10.0,200.0); Ball(60.0,45.0,0.0,10.0,5.0); Brick(new Rect(50.0,50.0,20.0,10.0),1,true); lives=3; after tick(0.1), the same brick has 0 hit points, getBricks() is empty, score is 100, and levelCompleted is true
- the exact life-loss fixture uses the same dimensions and paddle, Ball(100.0,199.0,0.0,20.0,5.0), an unbreakable Brick(new Rect(0.0,20.0,20.0,10.0),1,false), and 3 lives; after tick(0.5), lives is 2, lifeLost is true, ball x is 100.0, ball y is 174.0, ball vy is negative, and levelCompleted is false because the unbreakable brick remains
- MainTest contains exactly three concise deterministic tests: Main.main smoke, the exact injected one-brick fixture, and the exact injected life-loss fixture; the two domain tests MUST copy every numeric constructor argument and dt above literally, with no alternate dimensions, positions, velocities, radius, paddle, brick, or time step
- MainTest's life test must literally assert assertEquals(2,game.getLives()), assertTrue(game.isLifeLost()), assertEquals(100.0,ball.getX(),1e-9), assertEquals(174.0,ball.getY(),1e-9), assertTrue(ball.getVy()<0.0), and assertFalse(game.isLevelCompleted()); approximate phrases such as "positioned to cross" are insufficient and alternative fixtures are forbidden
- MainTest's brick test must literally use the stated 200.0-world fixture and tick(0.1), then assert the same Brick identity has zero hit points, game.getBricks().isEmpty(), score 100, and levelCompleted true; createDemoLevel and any substituted fixture are forbidden in this test
- retained Brick identity means only that the caller's original `brick` reference observes brick.getHitPoints()==0 after Game mutates and removes it; after removal the brick list MUST NOT contain that object, so the test must use assertFalse(game.getBricks().contains(brick)); asserting both isEmpty() and contains(brick), or otherwise asserting contains(brick) after removal, is explicitly forbidden
- the Game.java task and Full API must spell the reset expression as ball.setPosition(paddle.getX(),paddle.getY()-ball.getRadius()-1.0); examples using -0.1, paddle.getX()+paddle.getWidth()/2.0, a preserved old ball x, or any alternative formula are forbidden
- repeat the exact constructor, center-based Paddle semantics, mutable private int lives field, mandatory lives -= 1 bottom-out statement and reset coordinates, retained entity identity observed through the external brick reference, mandatory assertFalse after brick removal, read-only brick list, tick order, inclusive collision, score/removal rule, bricks-empty completion rule, coordinate convention, literal test assertions, and both numeric fixtures in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 39 functions or methods
- about 628 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- ball motion
- paddle control
- wall paddle and brick collision
- brick durability or removal
- score and lives
- level completion and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Implementation uses nearest-point-on-rect clamping and squared distance check. penetration() requires that an intersection exists; it returns new double[]{penX, penY} where penX = max(0, r - abs(cx - clamp(cx, rect.left(), rect.right()))), penY = max(0, r - abs(cy - clamp(cy, rect.top(), rect.bottom()))). These are magnitudes only. Callers choose the axis with the smaller magnitude to reflect velocity. In exact ties, callers may prefer Y-axis reflection for determinism.\\n\\nsrc/main/java/Game.java: public final class Game { private final double width,height; private final Paddle paddle; private final Ball ball; private final java.util.List<Brick> bricks; private int lives; int score; boolean levelCompleted; boolean lifeLost; public Game(double width, double height, Paddle paddle, Ball ball, java.util.List<Brick> bricks, int lives); public int getLives(); public boolean isLifeLost(); public boolean isLevelCompleted(); public int getScore(); public java.util.List<Brick> getBricks(); public Paddle getPaddle(); public Ball getBall(); public void tick(double dt); Semantics and rules: - Constructor: stores width/height; keeps references to the given paddle and ball; makes a defensive copy of the provided bricks list while retaining object identities, in insertion order; lives>=0. getBricks() returns an unmodifiable view of the internal list. - tick(dt): Validates dt is finite and > 0; otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException. Collision processing order: (1) walls (left/right/top reflection, bottom-out life loss), (2) paddle, (3) bricks (first-hit only). Walls: inclusive checks against bounds [0,width]x[0,height]. Left/right: if ball.x - r <= 0 reflect vx = -vx and clamp ball.x = r; if ball.x + r >= width reflect vx and clamp ball.x = width - r. Top: if ball.y - r <= 0 reflect vy and clamp ball.y = r. On each call, resets lifeLost=false. Integrates the ball exactly once: ball.x += ball.vx * dt; ball.y += ball.vy * dt. Collision processing order: (1) walls (left/right/top reflection, bottom-out life loss), (2) paddle, (3) bricks (first-hit only). Walls: inclusive checks against bounds [0,width]x[0,height]. Left/right: if ball.x - r <= 0 reflect vx = -vx and clamp ball.x = r; if ball.x + r >= width reflect vx and clamp ball.x = width - r. Top: if ball.y - r <= 0 reflect vy and clamp ball.y = r. Bottom-out: if ball.y - r >= height then a life is lost: decrement lives exactly by 1 (but not below 0), set lifeLost=true, and reset ball state as follows: position x := paddle.getX(), y := paddle.getY() - paddle.getHeight()/2 - ball.getRadius() (exactly tangent above the paddle); velocity vx := 0; vy := -Math.abs(previous vy). No further collisions are processed in this tick when bottom-out occurs. Paddle collision: compute paddleRect = paddle.asRect(); if Collision.circleIntersectsRect(ball.x,ball.y,r,paddleRect) reflect along min-penetration axis. Resolution: obtain {penX,penY} = Collision.penetration(...). If penY <= penX reflect vertical (vy = -vy) and translate ball out along Y by penY in the sign away from the paddle; else reflect horizontal (vx = -vx) and translate along X accordingly. Bricks collision: iterate over a snapshot copy of the bricks list and handle the first brick for which there is an intersection similarly: reflect along min-penetration axis, call brick.hit(), and if brick.isBreakable() and brick.isDestroyed() then remove the brick from the internal list and increase score by exactly 100. Level completion: levelCompleted is true iff all remaining bricks in the list are either non-breakable or destroyed (i.e., there are no remaining breakable and non-destroyed bricks). Flags and getters: getBricks() returns an unmodifiable list; lifeLost reflects only the outcome of the most recent tick; score is cumulative; getLives() returns current lives.
